counterfactual_missing_items: No CD30 expression or waxing-and-waning/self-regressing course is documented to support lymphomatoid papulosis
R4 supply no bone marrow or PCR clonal match evidence for its proposed subtype
The CD4-low/CD8-dominant phenotype is not explained by isolated lymphomatoid papulosis
decisive_items: Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal (20x magnification)
Lymphocytes positive for CD3, inverted CD8:CD4 ratio, predominantly α/β positive
T-cell receptor PCR: Matching clonal rearrangements identified in 3 skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample
response.rationale: C1 inherits and completes R3: the dermal papules, lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and clonal marrow-matched TCR rearrangements establish mycosis fungoides, while the CD4-depleted/CD8-dominant immunophenotype adds the CD8+ subtype. R3 is a sharp broad version but lacks the CD8-specific discriminator; R4 is unsupported because its two selected spans are shared with MF and there is no CD30/self-resolving waxing course to favor lymphomatoid papulosis.

rejected.why: Only dermal papules and lymphohistiocytic infiltrate are matched; no clonal skin-marrow PCR match, no CD8-predominant immunophenotype, and no CD30/regressing-course data would support lymphomatoid papulosis over mycosis fungoides.
